text:
Maya: Heads up — production error spike in us-west-2 around 09:05 UTC, lots of model pulls failing with connection resets.\/\/ traced to egress errors from edge fleet.
Sam: What are the error codes? 502/504 or TCP resets?
Maya: both. example from a node: 
```\ncurl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer\n\n# netstat snapshot on the host\n$ netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l\n61512\n```
Zoe: 61k TIME_WAIT is a lot — could be ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT gateway. Any CloudWatch spikes?
Maya: Yeah. NATGateway active connections ~64k and outbound error rate jumped. CloudWatch metric NATGateway:PortMappingCount at ceiling.
Priya: That's consistent with a fanout during model bootstrap — when nodes start they pull models concurrently, each opens many short connections.
Sam: Did we recently roll a new AMI or change concurrency?
Maya: We rolled new sidecar last night that doesn't reuse connections well (no keep-alive). Also autoscaler kicked 50 new agents at once for a batch job. Bad timing.
Jeff: Quick check — AWS NAT gateway uses ephemeral port mappings per source IP. If the mapping limit per NAT IP (64k) is hit you see exactly this. Each TCP connection consumes one ephemeral port mapping while in TIME_WAIT.
Zoe: Short-term mitigations: 1) add additional NAT gateways in other AZs and update route tables, 2) create S3 VPC endpoint to offload model pulls, 3) rate-limit model pulls during scale-ups.
Maya: Spun up 2 extra NAT gateways in the affected AZ and added route table entries. Requesting PR to add an S3 gateway endpoint now.
Sam: Can we also patch the sidecar to enable HTTP keep-alive and connection pooling? That should dramatically reduce new connections.
Priya: Yes — sidecar change is low-risk. Will open a canary PR that sets Connection: keep-alive and connection pool size to 100.
Jeff: Also consider increasing host ephemeral range and reducing TIME_WAIT on the nodes while we fix the app:
```\n# temp (tested on staging)\nsysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"20000 65535\"\nsysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30\n```
But that's only a bandaid and can hurt NAT mapping density. Prefer server-side keepalive.
Maya: Agreed. Implementing keepalive + S3 endpoint + extra NATs is current plan.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0329-01 - NAT gateway port exhaustion in us-west-2. Paging oncall.
Sam: Other medium-term ideas: per-AZ caching (local registry for models), pre-bake larger base AMIs with commonly used models, or host models behind PrivateLink so we bypass NAT entirely.
Zoe: Also evaluate using NAT instances with enhanced port mapping if needed, or use AWS Gateway Load Balancer to scale NATs. But those add ops burden.
Priya: I'll throttle the autoscaler to avoid big parallel startups until we have the sidecar change.
Maya: Rolling the autoscaler throttle now.
Jeff: For postmortem we should capture: timeline, root cause (sidecar not reusing connections + concurrent boots), immediate mitigations, and longer-term fixes (keepalive, VPC endpoints, local cache).
Sam: Can someone add a dashboard widget for NAT Gateway Port Utilization and TIME_WAIT count per fleet? That would help alert earlier.
Maya: On it, creating grafana panel and an alarm at 50k TIME_WAIT.
Zoe: Action items summary:
- Maya: Grafana panel + incident notes
- Priya: Sidecar keep-alive PR + throttle autoscaler
- Sam: S3 VPC endpoint PR and route updates
- Jeff: Draft postmortem template and alternatives (PrivateLink, local cache)
- Ops: keep extra NAT gateways until safe
Maya: Thanks all — systems trending back to normal after NAT additions and throttles. Will update after sidecar canary completes. :thumbsup:
